source.title: A modified Adam algorithm for deep neural network optimization
source.authors: M. Reyad; Amany M. Sarhan; M. Arafa

record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizers on image-classification test accuracy, a different measure and setting from the cited optimizer-generalization comparisons.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own test-accuracy comparisons for CNNs trained with several optimizers on MNIST and CIFAR-10. ImageNet comparisons in Table 7 are stated to be taken from other work, so they are not extracted as results. The cited EVGO architecture results are also prior-work results, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own adaptive-optimizer versus SGD test-accuracy comparisons on two CNN image-classification tasks, bearing on V4 in a new setting. Section 6 specifies fixed default hyperparameters, rather than an undocumented tuning protocol. The baseline comparisons test V4 even though the paper primarily proposes HN_Adam.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that HN_Adam improves Adam's generalization performance and reduces training time without increasing complexity, outperforming comparators on most reported measures. This is the authors' conclusion, rather than evidence of matched-training-performance generalization gains.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizers on CNN image classifiers with standard datasets and test accuracy; it does not state a limited-tuning protocol and proposes a modified Adam algorithm.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and optimizer change the reported test accuracy; the study reports results separately for MNIST and CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: HN_Adam improves reported accuracy and training time relative to comparator optimizers; additional own results evaluate LeNet-5, AlexNet, ResNet and ImageNet ResNet-18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed HN_Adam optimizer improves classifier performance in the evaluated configurations.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for test accuracy. The study does not document optimizer tuning limits, and its CIFAR-10 test-accuracy differences from SGD are small for Adam, AMSGrad, and RMSprop.
record.rows_left_out: No own-result rows were extracted from Table 7 because the text says the compared algorithms' results were taken from references [30, 66]. Cited EVGO results discussed in Remark 1 were also left out as prior-work results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width variation beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Learning-rate and decay-schedule searches, broader tuning, momentum-SGD comparisons, language benchmarks, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD. The fixed-default experiments do not establish an optimizer disadvantage after comparable optimization.
Batch-size variation, large-batch penalties, and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions; including dropout in an architecture does not test its effect.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Identification and removal of memorized training examples.

missing.what: Minimum training losses for the established optimizer comparisons: MNIST AdaBelief 1.48115, Adam 1.483735, AMSGrad 1.484545, SGD 2.296593, RMSprop 1.476105, AdaGrad 2.279421. All adaptive methods also attain lower training loss, so these results do not isolate a generalization advantage at matched training performance.

Minimum training losses for CIFAR-10: AdaBelief 0.0101, Adam 0.0292, AMSGrad 0.0281, SGD 0.0318, RMSprop 0.0577, AdaGrad 0.387. These distinguish optimization performance from held-out performance; notably RMSprop and AdaGrad have higher training loss but numerically higher test accuracy than SGD.

record.verdict_notes: Section 6 states defaults of learning rate 0.001, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.99 and epsilon 1e-8; the record incorrectly treats the tuning setup as wholly unspecified. Five runs are mentioned, but their aggregation and variability are not supplied. Table 7's comparator values are borrowed results and cannot provide an independent V4 test; its HN_Adam result is the authors' own. Remark 1 likewise mixes cited EVGO results with new HN_Adam results. The tranche correction reflects a new experimental setting; test accuracy is not a different measure from the original optimizer comparisons. These scoped counterexamples do not refute V4's frequency qualifier across benchmarks.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

The study does not state that tuning was limited to learning rates and decay schedules, does not compare equal or better training performance against held-out performance in a way that establishes a generalization gap, and does not test broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and batch-size variation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

relation.reason: Tables 3 and 5 report adaptive-optimizer and SGD test accuracies from the study's own experiments, independently of the proposed HN_Adam method's performance.

tranche.reason: The study reports its own established adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons on two CNN architectures under fixed default settings, providing new settings bearing on V4.

source_check.notes: The verdicts apply to these default-setting comparisons; they do not establish matched-training-performance differences or refute V4's broader 'often' claim. R1/R8 are method-evaluation results; ImageNet comparators are borrowed from prior work, and Table 5's AdaGrad accuracy should be retained despite the surrounding worst-performance wording.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: All reported adaptive optimizers exceed the SGD test accuracy (R2–R4, R6–R7); the study does not specify limited tuning, so this challenges the version only in the reported setup.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Adaptive optimizer values are above or nearly equal to SGD in these results, but the reported setup does not establish the limited-tuning condition or a training-to-test gap (R9–R14).
